chunks: Aban, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Statement of Allah, the Exalted and Mighty: 'In houses which Allah has permitted to be exalted,' he (peace be upon him) said: 'They are the houses of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.النَّبِيِّ: the Prophet (referring to the Prophets in general or specifically Muhammad and his family)
key_terms.بُيُوتٍ: houses (plural of bayt, referring to dwelling places or specific locations)
key_terms.تُرْفَعَ: be exalted/raised (passive verb, referring to elevation in status or physical building)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'houses which Allah has permitted to be exalted' refer to according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Abu Baseer asks Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about the meaning of the phrase 'In houses which Allah has permitted to be exalted' from the Quran. The Imam clarifies that these 'houses' refer specifically to the houses of the Prophets, highlighting the spiritual elevation of the Prophet Muhammad's household (Ahl al-Bayt) as the primary locus of divine worship and authority in Shia exegesis.

en.hubeali: H 14958 – Aban, from Abu Baseer who said:
I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Statement of Allahazwj: “[24:36] In houses which Allah has permitted to be exalted”, heasws said: ‘Houses of the Prophetsas’.
en.sarwar: 511. Aban, from Yahya Bin Abu Al-A’la who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (a.s.) saying: ‘The armour of the Rasool Allah (saww), Zat Al-Fuzoul had two rings of foil in front of it, and two rings of foil at the back of it’. And said; ‘Ali (a.s.) wore it on the Day of Al-Jamal’.
